objective: Traverse an immutable acyclic list recursively into a fresh array of original values.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Recursive linked-list traversal remains a current data-structure lesson.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Preserving shared values and caller ownership is useful in application transformations.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Null base cases and exact reference identity transfer to tree traversal.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: A bounded node chain fits the stated tier without unbounded stack promises.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Mutation, cloned values and fresh-empty tests prevent silent ownership violations.

defects: Acyclicity, finite depth and ownership guarantees were absent.
Cloning object values and destroying next pointers passed all prior cases.
Repeated suffix copying was not distinguished from the linear accumulator reveal.
rationale: Define at most 200 ordinary acyclic nodes ending in null, frozen nodes and opaque values including undefined. Add frozen nested/object identities, fresh empty and repeated outputs, and a 200-node order boundary. State the taught suffix-copying O(n²) model and accept the O(n) accumulator alternative/reveal. All supplied and alternative recursions pass; destructive and cloning implementations now fail.
